11	Proposal to collapse Connectors + Models + Sandboxes + Devices into one surface at `/connect/*`. Designed 2026-07-27, **not built**. Spec artifact: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/eb23eeaf-922a-4e9e-b9dd-56a73bf6baa4
12	
13	**Why it holds up (structural evidence, not taste):**
14	- `DeviceWorkerItem` already lives in `packages/owletto/src/lib/api/connections.ts` — not a devices module — and carries `connector_count`, `connector_error_count`, `connectors[]`.
15	- `AgentProviderCatalogItem` (`lib/api/agents.ts`) has `installed`, `authType`, `description`, `iconUrl` — near-identical to `ConnectorDefinitionItem`.
16	- `SandboxItem.connected` means "required credential exists in the vault" — the same question `connection.status` answers.
17	- All four are: browse a catalog → authenticate → get an instance → watch it run. The split is four pages that grew separately and got a shared `ConnectTabBar` bolted on later (`src/lib/connect-tabs.ts` already calls the group "Connect").
18	
19	**FINAL SHAPE 2026-07-27 (3rd revision).** Two tabs inside the single "Connect" sidebar row:
20	- **Connectors** — what an agent can reach. Device-provided connectors (Screen Time, Photos, Bookmarks) ALSO listed here read-only with their host named ("via Burak's MacBook"); not-addable and not-listed are different things.
21	- **Runtime** — devices + sandboxes (this merge is well-founded and cheap).
22	- **No status/attention tab** — broken rows sort to the top of their own tab; a dedicated tab would sit empty.
23	- **Models LEAVES the tab bar** — a tab advertises a required setup step, and models are optional on SaaS (`hasSystemKey()`); reached just-in-time via `agent-error-cta.ts`. CAVEAT: `hasSystemKey()` is deployment state — self-hosted OSS may have NO platform key, making Models step one. Evidence-gated, see below.
24	
25	**Sidebar reality (I got this wrong for most of the session):** `OWNER_SECTIONS` has exactly TWO entries — Memory and Connect (`segments: ["connectors","infrastructure"]`) — then an Agents roster, then Recent. Connect is ONE row above the roster, framed in-code as "workspace plumbing". So the "does this read as an agent harness?" worry is a non-issue; everything designed here lives inside one sidebar row.
26	
27	**UNRESOLVED — external MCP clients under Runtime.** Adversarial review rejected it: devices/sandboxes are substrates Lobu *dispatches work onto*; an MCP client *initiates requests into* Lobu — authorized, not provisioned. "Where it runs" is literally false for it. Also mixes resource instances (Burak's MacBook) with client classes (Claude Code). Proposed compromise: stateless **setup recipes** can live in Runtime (`DeviceTarget` and MCP `InstallTarget` are the same shape, and `lobu login` is already both); stateful **connected client instances** belong in an Access/Connected-clients surface. Hinges on whether users read an MCP client as "where my agent works from" or "a thing I granted access to" — not a code question.
28	
29	**User decisions — what SURVIVES the revision:** landing shows what's CONNECTED (not catalog-first); **deployments fold-in goes FIRST**. What does NOT survive: the full `/connect/*` move (dropped — largest work, least evidence, and the win was tidiness) and "uniform rows, kind is a label" (too strong — a device row NAVIGATES, a sandbox row does not; uniform *appearance*, not uniform *behaviour*).
30	
31	**Merge the LIST, keep DETAIL views distinct** — connections/feeds, API keys/model lists, permissions/pairing are genuinely different shapes.
32	
33	**The five-state vocabulary is WRONG — superseded 2026-07-27 (external review, accepted).** working/attention/installed-idle/available/managed collapses THREE orthogonal axes: **provisioning** (available|installed), **health** (working|attention), **ownership** (self|managed). They vary independently, so the enum cannot express "managed AND failing" (a delegated connector whose owning org revoked it — real), "degraded/partial" (1 of 2 Slack workspaces expired), pending/validating, rate-limited, or stale/unknown. Model the four fields separately and DERIVE the row label. A new case then adds a derivation, not a 6th enum value every surface must re-handle.
34	
35	**Model + sandbox detail pages are FLAT — no tabs.** A credential + a short list is one subject. Tabs only where there is genuinely more than one (connector: Overview/Feeds/Actions/Settings; device: Runs/Connectors/Permissions). Sharpens the open question: neither may deserve a route at all — both could be drawers on the list.
36	
37	**Blast radius is the one addition that makes this superior rather than tidier.** Show what depends on each row ("12 agents", "4 behaviors") and sort attention rows BY it — a rejected model key outranks an offline laptop. Severity is a property of what sits downstream, not of the row. Without it a merged list is an inventory; with it, it is triage.
38	
39	**Blockers / traps:**
40	- `chrome-extension` is NOT in the frontend platform union (`ios|android|macos|windows|linux`) — 4 Chrome connectors won't typecheck until widened.
41	- The rail means two things: on a connector it drills INTO children (connections); on models/devices it switches between SIBLINGS. Same position, different relation.
42	- Two rail sides exist today: connector pages use a LEFT rail; the device page uses a 360px RIGHT sidebar. Merging forces one (left).
43	- Kind vs facet are different axes — "chat" is what it does, "device" is where it runs. WhatsApp is both (cloud API + local Mac). A row must be allowed in two buckets.
44	- Device rows are two different things: "Lobu for Mac" is the runtime you install, "Reminders" is a connector it provides. Flat listing makes the app look like a peer of what it hosts.
45	- The built-in sandbox must NOT be a row — it's in `SandboxesPayload` but the current page never renders it. Listing it invites a "disconnect" that isn't real.
46	- "Managed" state (someone else owns the credential): public-org delegated connectors, `systemAvailable` model keys, cross-org device grants. Each surface answers this differently today; a merge forces one answer.
47	
48	**Rail is one tree across 3 levels** (connector → connection → feed) and descending "only moves the highlight" — `$connectorKey.$connectionId.tsx` renders the same `ConnectorSourcesRail`. Feeds belong to the CONNECTION, not the connector. This survives the merge unchanged.
49	
50	**Route name is `create`, NOT `add`** — `/$owner/connectors/create` + `create.$connectorKey.tsx` already exist. Page title is "Add a connection".
51	
52	**Install ≠ connect.** `install_connector` enables a DEFINITION and explicitly "does not authenticate external accounts"; `connect` separately creates a connection. Takes exactly ONE of `connector_id` | `source_url` | `source_uri` | `source_code` | `mcp_url`. The web UI exposes two via ONE auto-detecting field: URLs ending `.ts`/`.js` → `source_url`, anything else → probed as `mcp_url` (`connection-form.tsx:804-846`). `source_uri`/`source_code` are CLI/agent only.
53	
54	**Clicking an uninstalled catalog connector shows a PREVIEW screen with an explicit install button** (`use-installable-connector-selection.ts`): `installed === false && installable` → preview → install from the catalog entry's `source_uri` → reload catalog → verify it came back installed → THEN configuration. Already-installed connectors skip straight to configure. Failure path: a catalog entry with no `source_uri` errors "missing a source URI".
55	
56	**Sandbox add = provider dropdown + that provider's fields.** `PROVIDER_FIELDS` in `$owner/environments/index.tsx`: default is a single `apiKey`; `vercel` needs `token`+`teamId`+`projectId`. That's the whole flow — hence the sandbox subpage is probably a drawer, not a route.
57	
58	**Device pairing already exists** in `src/components/devices/device-connect.tsx` — THREE runtimes, not two: macOS app (PRIVATE BETA → "Contact us", `MAC_CONTACT_URL = https://lobu.ai/schedule`), Chrome extension ("Add to Chrome", real web store link), CLI (`npm i -g @lobu/cli && lobu login`). Three different verbs; a single "Install" label would be wrong. User's idea: surface these in the device rail as "Bring your own" under the paired devices.
59	
60	**Device connectors (Screen Time, Photos…) are not CATALOG rows** — they AUTO-WIRE when a paired device advertises the capability, so an "Add" button would have nothing to do. The catalog lists the 3 runtimes instead. **BUT they must still be VISIBLE under Connectors** with their device named (revised 2026-07-27): a user asking "what can my agent read" looks in Connectors, and hiding them only under Runtime means searching "Screen Time" finds nothing. Not-addable and not-listed are different things — this was the hole in the original three-tab split.
61	
62	## The narrow "Runtime" cut — DO THIS FIRST (session f79c5bac, verified 2026-07-27)
63	
64	Fold **Sandboxes + Devices → one "Runtime" tab**. Connect goes 4 tabs → 3: **Connectors, Models, Runtime** = what you connect to, what thinks, where it runs. ~4 files changed, 2 new. Ships value without waiting on the permission question, and de-risks the full merge by proving its two hard problems cheaply.
65	
66	Why it's coherent: the two ledes already say the same thing from opposite ends — sandboxes are "remote sandbox providers your agents can execute in *instead of the built-in local runtime*"; devices "run device-bound connectors". Remote vs local runtime. Both already render through the same `InfraTabScaffold`.
67	
68	**The asymmetry — a device row NAVIGATES, a sandbox row does NOT:**
69	| | Devices | Sandboxes |
70	|---|---|---|
71	| Row | `<Link>` → `devices/$deviceId` | `<div>` + inline delete/confirm |
72	| Add | `DeviceConnect` (pairing) | `CreateSandboxForm` (credential) |
73	| Scope | user-private, cross-workspace | org-scoped |
74	| Detail | separate route | expands in place |
75	
76	So "uniform rows" means uniform **appearance**, not uniform **behaviour**. Sort devices first (they already have a "Yours · private" badge) above org sandboxes.
77	
78	**Verified traps (re-checked against the repo, not taken on trust):**
79	- `InfraTabScaffold` takes ONE `addLabel: string` + ONE `onStartAdd: () => void` + one empty state. Two kinds = two Add flows. Extend it with an action array (Models still needs the single-action form) or drop it here.
80	- **Second mount point:** `SandboxesBody` is DEFINED in `$owner/environments/index.tsx` and imported by `infrastructure/sandboxes.tsx`. A merge scoped to `/infrastructure` leaves `/environments` on the old surface.
81	- `?provider=` deep link: `sandboxes.tsx` has `validateSearch` + auto-opens the create form with a prefill banner. New route needs the same, and the redirect must FORWARD the param.
82	- Independent empty states — "No runtimes" with a paired Mac but no Modal credential is a lie. Empty only when BOTH are.
83	- `src/app/index.tsx` hand-builds a device-detail URL → redirects from both old paths are mandatory. `routeTree.gen.ts` regenerates. `all-routes.test.tsx` + `owner-root-redirect.test.tsx` both need updating.
84	
85	
86	## Verified backend facts (re-checked 2026-07-27; two of these correct earlier claims)
87	
88	- **Connected MCP clients ALREADY have list + revoke.** `DELETE /mcp/:clientId` at `packages/server/src/lobu/client-routes.ts:302`, plus `lobu clients revoke` in the CLI (kills tokens AND live sessions). I had claimed "no revoke route" — that was over-generalised from the PAT case and is WRONG for OAuth clients. Only the **web UI** is missing.
89	- **PATs are a different asset class.** `PersonalAccessTokenService.revoke()` at `auth/tokens.ts:174` with no HTTP route found. Do not collapse PATs, OAuth clients and messaging identities into one list — messaging identities deliberately have NO revoke (they are platform users).
90	- **Devices are ORG-attached, not user-private.** `DeviceWorkerItem` carries `organization_id` and NO `user_id`; the comment says "Workspace this device is attached to". The "Yours · private / follows you across workspaces" grouping came from a prior session's summary and I repeated it in two artifacts unverified. Group Runtime by KIND.
91	- **MCP install registry already exists, hidden.** `mcp-install-targets.ts` has 6 targets (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, ChatGPT, Gemini CLI, Skills) + `buildMcpUrl(orgSlug)` → `/mcp/{slug}`. Used in exactly ONE place: a line inside `device-connect.tsx`. `DeviceTarget` and `InstallTarget` are the SAME shape — collapse them.
92	- **Dynamic client registration** at `POST /oauth/register` (documented at `GET /auth.md`) — no allowlist, so "custom MCP client" is instructions, not a record you create.
93	- **Routes that break on a rename** (all invisible to a refactor, must be repointed FIRST): `infrastructure.tsx:8` redirects bare `/infrastructure` → `sandboxes` (a route being deleted); `agent-error-cta.ts:72` builds `/{slug}/infrastructure/models` — that IS the just-in-time path the plan depends on; `app/index.tsx:108` string-concatenates a device URL.
94	- **Second double-mount found:** `InferenceProvidersBody` is defined in `inference-providers/index.tsx` and re-mounted at `infrastructure/models` — same trap as `SandboxesBody` in `environments/index.tsx`.
95	
96	**Agent binding over MCP is attribution only** — see [[project_mcp_binding_is_attribution_not_authz]]. This is the most serious finding of the session and gates the connected-clients UI.

# Behavior × Skill: merge into "live skills"? — Decision + what to build instead

## Context

Question asked: should Behavior and Skill merge into one concept ("live skills" — a skill with a trigger), with nix settings moving off skills since Behavior already has "Runs on", and Behavior deprecated? Prompted by: (a) nix settings on skills feeling misplaced, (b) the upcoming dynamic sandbox provider making per-run env provisioning possible.

Method: read-only study — codebase verification (done inline against source), market survey of ~15 products (Claude Skills, OpenClaw, Devin, Zapier Agents, Lindy, Dust, n8n, Val Town, Modal, Inngest, Trigger.dev, GitHub Actions, Temporal, Cloudflare Workers), adversarial for/against debate, judge. Judge verdict and my own verification converged.

## Verdict: do NOT merge, do NOT rename. Fix the provisioning path instead.

The originating itch is real, but it points at a **provisioning bug**, not an entity merge. "Runs on" answers WHERE a behavior executes; `nixPackages` answers WHAT must be present for a skill's content to work. Different axes — moving nix to Behavior would break skills used interactively in chat, where no behavior is in the loop at all.

### Why not merge (4 grounds)

1. **User-intent test fails.** A skill = "how to do X" (teach: install, enable, edit, carry between agents). A behavior = "when to act unprompted" (delegate: trigger, runs, windows, cooldown, notifications, pause). "Live skill" is "how AND when" — a conjunction, not a category. (Same standing rule that killed the Models-into-Connect merge: merge by user intent, not struct similarity.)
2. **Skills have no entity to merge into.** `SkillConfig` is per-agent jsonb (`agents.settings.skills_config`), no table, no org identity, no versioning. Watchers have versions, runs, classifiers, reactions, keying, notification config. A merge must first *invent* an org-level skill entity, then migrate the hot-path `watchers` table into it — a union type wearing a single table.
3. **Deprecating "Behavior" is a breaking product rename** — 16 MCP `manage_behaviors` actions, the enforced naming gate in `make pre-pr`, docs, UI routes — for zero functional payoff. It also relitigates the settled "unified Behaviors list, separate engines" decision.
4. **Market evidence is one-directional.** The SKILL.md ecosystem Lobu's skills byte-for-byte target (Claude Skills, agentskills.io, OpenClaw) keeps capability separate from automation and puts deps ON the skill (OpenClaw `requires.bins`). Runtime products attach env to the code unit, placement to the run: Modal `image=` on the function, GH Actions `runs.using` on the action vs `runs-on` on the workflow job, Trigger.dev `machine` on the task. Products that DID fuse triggers (Zapier Agents' "behaviors", Lindy, Dust, Notion) attach them to the **agent** — the shape Lobu already has. No surveyed product merged skill-level capability with automation.

## Ground truth (verified against source this session)

- Skill = SKILL.md-shaped capability: `SkillConfig` — `repo`, `content`, `nixPackages`, `providers`, `modelPreference`, `thinkingLevel`, pre-tool guardrails (`packages/core/src/contracts/agent-settings.ts:102-121`); stored per-agent (`packages/server/src/lobu/stores/postgres-stores.ts:174`).
- Skill nix is a **declaration of intrinsic deps**, unioned into the agent's `nixConfig` at CLI apply time (`packages/cli/src/commands/_lib/apply/map-config.ts:296-305`; doctrine comment `packages/cli/src/config/define.ts:596-598`); embedded worker spawns under `nix-shell -p <union>` (`packages/server/src/gateway/orchestration/deployment-manager.ts:2081-2118`).
- **The gap (the real bug):** the union is an apply-time snapshot. Skills enabled via UI/catalog/API write only `skills_config` — nothing recomputes `nixConfig`, so their nix never reaches provisioning; disabled skills keep contributing stale packages until the next `lobu apply`.
- Behavior "Runs on" = `device_worker_id` + `agent_kind` + `execution_config` (`packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_behaviors/crud.ts:252-278`; UI picker `packages/owletto/src/components/entity-tabs/watchers-tab/from-scratch-panel.tsx:1183`). `BehaviorExecutionConfig` is device-worker CLI flags only — timeout, budget, model, permission_mode, effort, finalize_nudges — **no env/deps field** (`packages/core/src/contracts/tools/manage-behaviors.ts:112-171`).
- Config doctrine already states the split: "Agent binding for a chat connection is a Behavior with a channel trigger, not an agent-scoped field" (`define.ts:568-573`). Listen is already Behavior rows (`behavior_channel_subscriptions`); `scheduled_jobs` stays a separate engine.

## What to build instead (staged)

### Stage 1 — per-spawn env union (the executable work item)
Compute the worker env at spawn/run time as `agent.nixConfig.packages ∪ enabled skills' nixPackages` instead of trusting the apply-time snapshot:
- Embedded path: `deployment-manager.ts` reads agent settings at spawn — add the union there (reuse `nixPackageAttrRef` sanitizer).
- Dynamic sandbox provider (when it lands): same union feeds the per-run sandbox spec. This is the "bring sandbox provider dynamically" hook — env becomes per-run derived state, owned by neither skill nor behavior.
- CLI apply keeps writing the union for back-compat, but runtime stops depending on it.
- Decide conflict semantics (skill A wants `python311`, skill B `python312`) — currently undefined; minimum: dedupe + log conflict, last-write-wins is not acceptable silently.
- Rollout note: this silently changes env for existing agents (UI-installed skills START contributing; disabled-after-apply skills STOP). Ship behind an explicit changelog entry, not as an incidental.

### Stage 2 — only on demonstrated need
Optional `nix_packages` on `BehaviorExecutionConfig` for behavior-specific deps no skill declares (e.g. `reaction_script` binaries). Additive, no migration. Do not build preemptively.

### Stage 3 — optional, UI-only
Surface skills in the unified Behaviors projection as a "runs: on demand" facet (same merged-projection precedent as Listen/Watch/Schedule). No data-model change. This is the sanctioned answer if "which one do I use" confusion shows up — not the merge.

### Parked (tracked decision, not rediscovery)
Skill anemia is real: no versioning, no org identity, no cross-agent sharing. If that pain grows, the fix is an org-level skill entity — a separate product decision, deliberately NOT bundled here (avoids the GitHub-Actions two-rich-peers tax).

## Explicitly not doing
- No Behavior↔Skill merge; no "live skills" rename; naming gate untouched.
- No moving nix skill→behavior (breaks chat/interactive skill use, breaks skill portability).
- No folding `scheduled_jobs` or Listen bindings into anything.
- No org-level skills table "while in there".

## Risks
1. Per-spawn union is a silent env change for existing agents — needs the explicit rollout note above.
2. Conflict semantics must be decided before Stage 1 ships.
3. Skill anemia pressure will resurface as merge pressure — answer with the parked entity decision, not the merge.

## Verification (Stage 1)
Red→fix→green per repo rules: integration test — agent with a UI-enabled skill declaring `nixPackages` → spawned worker env includes the package (red today); disable the skill → next spawn excludes it; conflict case logs and dedupes. Then `make pre-pr`, boot the embedded worker, exercise the spawn path live.

## Final step
Record the decision in auto-memory (behavior-skill merge REJECTED, Stage-1 env-union direction) so future sessions don't relitigate.

3. **Deprecating "Behavior" is a breaking product rename** — 16 MCP `manage_behaviors` actions, the enforced naming gate in `make pre-pr`, docs, UI routes — for zero functional payoff. It also relitigates the settled "unified Behaviors list, separate engines" decision.
4. **Market evidence is one-directional.** The SKILL.md ecosystem Lobu's skills byte-for-byte target (Claude Skills, agentskills.io, OpenClaw) keeps capability separate from automation and puts deps ON the skill (OpenClaw `requires.bins`). Runtime products attach env to the code unit, placement to the run: Modal `image=` on the function, GH Actions `runs.using` on the action vs `runs-on` on the workflow job, Trigger.dev `machine` on the task. Products that DID fuse triggers (Zapier Agents' "behaviors", Lindy, Dust, Notion) attach them to the **agent** — the shape Lobu already has. No surveyed product merged skill-level capability with automation.

## Ground truth (verified against source this session)

- Skill = SKILL.md-shaped capability: `SkillConfig` — `repo`, `content`, `nixPackages`, `providers`, `modelPreference`, `thinkingLevel`, pre-tool guardrails (`packages/core/src/contracts/agent-settings.ts:102-121`); stored per-agent (`packages/server/src/lobu/stores/postgres-stores.ts:174`).
- Skill nix is a **declaration of intrinsic deps**, unioned into the agent's `nixConfig` at CLI apply time (`packages/cli/src/commands/_lib/apply/map-config.ts:296-305`; doctrine comment `packages/cli/src/config/define.ts:596-598`); embedded worker spawns under `nix-shell -p <union>` (`packages/server/src/gateway/orchestration/deployment-manager.ts:2081-2118`).
- **The gap (the real bug):** the union is an apply-time snapshot. Skills enabled via UI/catalog/API write only `skills_config` — nothing recomputes `nixConfig`, so their nix never reaches provisioning; disabled skills keep contributing stale packages until the next `lobu apply`.
- Behavior "Runs on" = `device_worker_id` + `agent_kind` + `execution_config` (`packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_behaviors/crud.ts:252-278`; UI picker `packages/owletto/src/components/entity-tabs/watchers-tab/from-scratch-panel.tsx:1183`). `BehaviorExecutionConfig` is device-worker CLI flags only — timeout, budget, model, permission_mode, effort, finalize_nudges — **no env/deps field** (`packages/core/src/contracts/tools/manage-behaviors.ts:112-171`).
- Config doctrine already states the split: "Agent binding for a chat connection is a Behavior with a channel trigger, not an agent-scoped field" (`define.ts:568-573`). Listen is already Behavior rows (`behavior_channel_subscriptions`); `scheduled_jobs` stays a separate engine.

## What to build instead (staged)

### Stage 1 — per-spawn env union (EXECUTION SCOPE — user confirmed)
Compute the worker env at spawn/run time as `agent.nixConfig.packages ∪ enabled skills' nixPackages` instead of trusting the apply-time snapshot:
- Embedded path: `deployment-manager.ts` reads agent settings at spawn — add the union there (reuse `nixPackageAttrRef` sanitizer).
- Dynamic sandbox provider (when it lands): same union feeds the per-run sandbox spec. This is the "bring sandbox provider dynamically" hook — env becomes per-run derived state, owned by neither skill nor behavior.
- CLI apply keeps writing the union for back-compat, but runtime stops depending on it.
- Decide conflict semantics (skill A wants `python311`, skill B `python312`) — currently undefined; minimum: dedupe + log conflict, last-write-wins is not acceptable silently.
- Rollout note: this silently changes env for existing agents (UI-installed skills START contributing; disabled-after-apply skills STOP). Ship behind an explicit changelog entry, not as an incidental.

### Stage 2 — only on demonstrated need
Optional `nix_packages` on `BehaviorExecutionConfig` for behavior-specific deps no skill declares (e.g. `reaction_script` binaries). Additive, no migration. Do not build preemptively.

### Stage 3 — optional, UI-only
Surface skills in the unified Behaviors projection as a "runs: on demand" facet (same merged-projection precedent as Listen/Watch/Schedule). No data-model change. This is the sanctioned answer if "which one do I use" confusion shows up — not the merge.

### Parked (tracked decision, not rediscovery)
Skill anemia is real: no versioning, no org identity, no cross-agent sharing. If that pain grows, the fix is an org-level skill entity — a separate product decision, deliberately NOT bundled here (avoids the GitHub-Actions two-rich-peers tax).

## Explicitly not doing
- No Behavior↔Skill merge; no "live skills" rename; naming gate untouched.
- No moving nix skill→behavior (breaks chat/interactive skill use, breaks skill portability).
- No folding `scheduled_jobs` or Listen bindings into anything.
- No org-level skills table "while in there".

## Risks
1. Per-spawn union is a silent env change for existing agents — needs the explicit rollout note above.
2. Conflict semantics must be decided before Stage 1 ships.
3. Skill anemia pressure will resurface as merge pressure — answer with the parked entity decision, not the merge.

## Verification (Stage 1)
Red→fix→green per repo rules: integration test — agent with a UI-enabled skill declaring `nixPackages` → spawned worker env includes the package (red today); disable the skill → next spawn excludes it; conflict case logs and dedupes. Then `make pre-pr`, boot the embedded worker, exercise the spawn path live.

## Final step
Record the decision in auto-memory (behavior-skill merge REJECTED, Stage-1 env-union direction) so future sessions don't relitigate.

I verified that against `origin/main` rather than taking the report at face value — it's a real pre-existing drop, and on `POST /agents` it meant the `nix` a caller supplied was persisted to the session and then silently discarded. Same root cause as the skill bug, so I fixed the class in one pass and confirmed the other two `resolveAgentOptions` callers already route through the builder correctly.

I also found and fixed a bug the fixer introduced: its version spread `settings.nixConfig` over the base config, so agent packages clobbered per-request packages wholesale. I proved it with a throwaway probe (`sessionpkg` vanished from the result) before changing anything. The union now covers all three sources, request-first and deduped.

**Resolution logic — high (~90).** Red→green is real: 3 pass/5 fail with the original helper, 22 pass/0 fail after. Both new guards mutation-tested — breaking the base-packages union fails 2 tests, removing the `enabled` filter fails 1.

I verified the payload field is now populated at the seam; I did *not* verify the package actually lands in the worker's environment. `make pre-pr` is clean, but that's build/typecheck/knip/lint only.

**The two payload-drop fixes — medium (~70).** Correct by inspection and typecheck, and structurally identical to what `buildMessagePayload` already does, but neither path has a test covering the lift.

## Suggested next actions

1. Live e2e: enable a skill with `nixPackages` through the UI, dispatch a run, confirm the binary is on `PATH` in the worker — this is the verification still owed.
2. Add a payload-level test asserting `nixConfig` reaches the top-level `MessagePayload` from both hand-rolled sites, so the drop can't regress.
3. Consider making `buildMessagePayload` the only way to enqueue — the two drops existed precisely because bypassing it is easy and silent.

The verdict came from your own question earlier this session, and it held up after the study. Short version: the two answer different questions, and the thing that made a merge feel necessary was a bug, not a modeling error.

**They fail the no-conjunction test.** A skill is "how to do X" — you teach it, enable it, edit it, carry it between agents. A behavior is "when to act unprompted" — trigger, runs, windows, cooldown, notifications, pause. "Live skill" is *how AND when*, which is a conjunction, not a category. That's the same rule that killed the Models-into-Connect merge: merge by user intent, not by struct similarity.

**Your "Runs on" premise pointed at a different axis than you expected.** I checked what "Runs on" actually is — `device_worker_id` + `agent_kind` + `execution_config`, and `execution_config` is CLI flags only (timeout, budget, model, permission_mode, effort), with no env or deps field at all. So "Runs on" answers *where* execution happens; `nixPackages` answers *what must exist for the skill's content to work*. Moving nix onto Behavior would break skills used in an ordinary chat turn, where no behavior is in the loop at all — the packages have to follow the skill everywhere it's used.

**There's no entity on the skill side to merge into.** `SkillConfig` is per-agent jsonb in `agents.settings.skills_config` — no table, no org identity, no versioning. Watchers have versions, runs, classifiers, reactions, keying, notification config. A merge would have to first invent an org-level skill entity, then migrate the hot-path `watchers` table into it, then rename 16 MCP actions and the `make pre-pr` naming gate — a union type wearing one table, for no functional gain.

**The market is one-directional on this.** The SKILL.md ecosystem your skills byte-for-byte target (Claude Skills, agentskills.io, OpenClaw's `requires.bins`) keeps deps on the capability. Runtime products do the same split you already have: Modal puts `image=` on the function, GitHub Actions puts `runs.using` on the action but `runs-on` on the job. And the products that *did* fuse triggers — Zapier Agents, Lindy, Dust — attach them to the **agent**, which is exactly Lobu's current shape.

**What the itch actually was.** Skill nix genuinely wasn't working, which is what made the model feel wrong. The union was an apply-time snapshot baked by `lobu apply`, so any skill enabled through the UI or catalog wrote only `skills_config` and its packages never reached provisioning. That's the fix that just merged — resolve-time union, no entity change. The two extra drops found along the way had the same signature.

One thing I'd flag as still open, since it's the likeliest source of renewed merge pressure: skills are genuinely anemic — no versioning, no org identity, no cross-agent sharing. If that pain grows, the answer is an org-level skill entity, not folding them into Behavior. Parked deliberately rather than bundled in.

content.text:
Yes — deployments exist and are genuinely good, but they don't close the skill-versioning gap. The distinction matters.

**What deployments actually are.** Each `lobu apply` mints an `apply_id`, stamps it on every config-audit event (`events` with `semantic_type='change'`, indexed by `metadata->>'apply_id'`), and posts a summary including a redacted desired-state **manifest** plus the config repo's HEAD SHA. `lobu rollback <apply_id>` re-applies that manifest through the same diff/execute engine, and `deployment_pause` stops a later CI apply from silently re-promoting over a deliberate rollback. That's real change tracking with real rollback.

**Why it doesn't cover skills.** It's scoped to the `lobu apply` path — config-as-code. The skill-anemia problem is precisely about skills that *don't* come through apply: enabled via the UI, the catalog, or the API. Those write straight to `agents.settings.skills_config` with no `apply_id`, no manifest entry, and no change event. That's the same seam as the bug just fixed — the CLI knew about skill nix, the UI path didn't.

So there are two populations. Apply-managed skills are versioned today, through the config repo's git history and the deployment manifest. UI-installed skills have no version, no history, no rollback. Deployments track *the apply*, not *the skill* — there's no skill identity to hang a version on, since a skill is a jsonb blob inside one agent's settings.

**Where this leaves the merge question.** It actually strengthens the case against merging. If deployments already give apply-managed config change-tracking and rollback, then folding skills into Behavior to get versioning would be solving through the wrong entity — you'd inherit watcher versioning for something whose real gap is that UI writes bypass the deployment path entirely.

The narrower fix, if you want to close it: make UI/catalog skill mutations emit the same `semantic_type='change'` events the apply path stamps, so they show up in the deployment/audit timeline even without an `apply_id`. That gets you history without inventing an entity. Full per-skill versioning and rollback still needs the org-level skill entity — which is the parked decision, and I'd still keep it parked until the pain is concrete.

Yes — largely what you're describing already works, with one real limitation. Verified rather than inferred this time:

**The skill definition does go into the deployment record.** `skillsConfig` is one of the diffed `SETTINGS_FIELDS` (`diff.ts:331`), and skills resolve *eagerly* at apply time — `skillFromFile` reads the `SKILL.md` off disk and inlines its `content` plus `nixPackages` into `SkillConfig` (`desired-state.ts:342-404`). That resolved state flows into `redactDesiredState`, which is stored as the deployment `manifest` and hashed as `manifest_hash`. So the full skill body, not just a file reference, is captured in the snapshot.

**That makes rollback work for skills.** Since the manifest is self-contained, `lobu rollback <apply_id>` re-applies the skill content as it was at that apply — you're not depending on the `SKILL.md` still existing at that path or that revision.

**The limitation: change detection is field-level, not value-level.** `diffSettings` compares `deepEqual(desired[field], remote?[field])` and pushes only the **field name** into `changedFields`. So a deployment tells you *"`skillsConfig` changed on agent X"* — it does not tell you which skill, or what changed inside it. Editing one line of one skill's markdown produces the same `changedFields: ["skillsConfig"]` as adding three new skills.

So to answer directly: you see *that* skills changed, and you can recover *what they became* (from the manifest) and diff two manifests yourself — but the deployment log itself doesn't render a per-skill or per-line change view.

Two caveats worth stating. This whole path is `lobu apply`-only; UI/catalog-installed skills still bypass it entirely, which is the anemia gap from earlier. And I checked the CLI-side construction, not the server-side deployment detail route — I haven't confirmed how the UI renders `changedFields`, so it's possible the surface is even coarser than the data.

If you want per-skill visibility, the cheap version is making `diffSettings` special-case `skillsConfig` to emit `skillsConfig.<name>` entries instead of the bare field name. That's a contained change to one function and needs no new entity — meaningfully smaller than the org-level skill entity, and it'd give you exactly the "what changed" view you're asking about.
